member.name: T:Interpreter.Models.PrecedencesLogicOperators
member.summary: Defines the precedence levels for logical operators. Lower integer values indicate higher precedence (tighter binding).
member.remarks:
v3.4: corrected to match the VHDL operator-precedence chart. Previously et al. had value 1 (highest precedence) while had 5 (lowest), which inverted the standard: `d = '1' and d_prev = '0'` parsed as `d = ('1' and d_prev) = '0'` and then threw "Type mismatch: expected BOOLEAN, got STD_LOGIC" downstream. The fix flips the bands so `=` binds tighter than `and`.
Reference (VHDL spec, highest precedence to lowest): 1. **, abs, not — value 0 2. *, /, mod, rem — value 1 (PrecedencesArithOperators) 3. + (sign), - (sign) — value 0 (PrecedencesArithOperators.UNARY) 4. + (binary), - (binary), & (concatenate) — value 2 5. sll, srl, sla, sra, rol, ror — value 3 6. =, /=, <, <=, >, >= — value 4 7. and, or, nand, nor, xor, xnor — value 5 8. assignment (<=, :=) — value 6

remarks.para: History: v0.17 deferred only edge-detection functions because their values depend on simulation state. v3.1 (#28) extends the list to every IEEE function the synthesizer has a primitive emitter for — otherwise to_integer / resize / shift_* / rotate_* still get inline-evaluated and the synth never sees a call to lower.

member.name: M:Interpreter.Program.JoinContinuationLines(System.String[])
member.summary: Joins physical VHDL source lines that belong to one logical statement before they reach the line-by-line state machine in .
member.remarks:
VHDL lacks an explicit continuation character — a statement is whatever runs from one terminator to the next, regardless of how many physical lines it spans. The downstream code uses string matching on individual lines (StartsWith("end "), Contains("function ... is"), etc.), so a statement broken across lines was silently mis-classified.
A line is considered "complete" when: • parenthesis depth has returned to 0, AND • the trailing token is one of: ;, is, then, else, elsif, loop, begin, generate, or record. Comments (-- to EOL) are stripped before the completion check but preserved in the joined output so downstream tooling that reads them still works.

member.summary: Coordinates VHDL delta cycle simulation. Manages the execution of concurrent statements with proper signal scheduling.

remarks.para: Delta cycle semantics:

list.item: All signal assignments within a delta cycle are scheduled, not immediate
At the end of each delta cycle, all scheduled updates are applied simultaneously
If any signal changes, processes sensitive to those signals are re-executed
This continues until no more signals change (simulation stabilizes)
Only then does simulation time advance

member.name: M:Interpreter.Services.Resources.CalculateLUTs
member.summary: Estimates LUT usage from combinational logic operations. Walks every Operation inside the architecture (concurrent assignments + everything nested in Process bodies, if-structures, case-structures, loops) and weights each operator by the result's bit width. Accuracy: ~60-80% (synthesis optimization affects this).
member.remarks:
Per-operator cost model (matches the guidance originally sketched as TODO comments in this method):
and / or / xor / nand / nor / xnor → 1 LUT × result_bits
not → 0 (inverters fold into LUT inputs for free on FPGAs)
+ / - → ~3 LUTs × result_bits (ripple-carry, matches Xilinx/Intel estimators)
* / / → 0 (mapped to DSP slices, counted by )
sll / srl / sla / sra / rol / ror → 1 LUT × result_bits (mux-chain)
= / /= / < / > / <= / >= → max(1, bits/2) LUTs per comparator

member.name: T:Interpreter.Synthesis.ProcessSynthesizer
member.summary: Lowers a VHDL into a netlist. The entry walks the process body and produces, per driven signal, a "value net" — the gated combinational expression that should drive the signal. Clocked processes wrap each value net in a DFF; pure combinational processes drive the named signal directly via a BUF.
member.remarks:
The walker handles three task kinds in process bodies:
— a plain x <= y assignment.
— if/elsif/else branches lower to a chain of MUX cells, one per branch, with the else (or "previous value" feedback) terminating the chain.
— each when clause becomes a disjunction of EQ comparators against the selector, then feeds a MUX in the same chain pattern as if/elsif.
Anything we can't decompose (loops, nested processes, statements we don't recognise) sends the whole process to the fallback so the diagram stays honest about what wasn't synthesised.
